answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places their Player ID card upright in its stand visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set with that color on its backs, remove cards targeting colors not in play, and keep each player's own Ambush. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four cards face down to the center with values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: IDs are upright in stands; remove cards targeting colors not playing; deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player voting turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed; once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and reveal choices simultaneously.

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is needed. The player or players receiving the most votes are the Target(s); with three votes for Red and two each for Blue and Green, Red alone is the Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.”

answers.answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes. Without successful Ambush protection, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive that requirement, subject to any applicable Ambush effects.
answers.evidence: Vote: tied players are all Targets; with tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated because Green did not vote for the Target, Blue, and did not successfully Ambush. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
answers.evidence: Resolve elimination: every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception.

answers.answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes, so the counted votes are Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds, so Red survives and may eliminate Yellow, the player who voted for Red. Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink remain.
answers.evidence: Ambush illustration: Red and Yellow tie as Targets; Yellow is eliminated; Red can retaliate only against Yellow; Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush lets the Target choose only one player who voted for them, even if four players did so. They cannot choose someone who voted for another color.
answers.evidence: Ambush: chooses “one of the players who voted for them”; cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.

answers.answer: That player eliminates themselves. An Ambush works only if its player is a Target in that vote.
answers.evidence: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, another Conspire and vote occurs among the surviving players.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: three or more survivors continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points; each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: one survivor collects “all four central Gold Bars.” Components: receiving one bar means one card valued at 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go cards; they may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card and places it face down. When both are ready, they reveal simultaneously and resolve the pairing.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown section: each takes Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; may discuss; choose one face down; reveal simultaneously when both are ready.

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar, including those eliminated in it. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave them for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: no survivors means each player not participating in final vote receives one deck bar; leave the four central bars and add no new bars. Special Rules clarifies final voters receive no consolation bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share/Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The Share player gets zero bars and the Steal player gets all four central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share against Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player gets one central bar, and the Steal player gets the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go against Steal: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player gets one central bar, and the Share player gets the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go against Share: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.”

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one bar; two remain in the center. If play continues, add two new bars to bring the central pool to four.
answers.evidence: Both Grab One & Go: each receives one, leave the other two central, and add just two new bars for the next round.

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Both Steal: neither finalist receives gold; every other player gets one deck bar; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after bars have been awarded. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring: check at end of round after awards; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; highest point total wins.

answers.answer: The booklet's instruction, as summarized, is that tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown and repeat as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. For exactly two tied players, that instruction is actionable using the two-player Showdown. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated earlier in the round; all IDs are stood upright for the next round.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeated as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total. Turn Structure: if no winner, everyone returns; stand all IDs upright.

answers.answer: Before every vote, players conspire for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, including secretly, texting, and showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
answers.evidence: Conspire: “for roughly a minute and a half at most”; communication may be open or secret, including texting and showing a Voting card; game owner asks for final decisions.

answers.answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the color of the target player's visible ID and place it face down in front of yourself. To defend yourself if you suspect you are the target, play your own Ambush card instead.
answers.evidence: Vote: place one card face down in front of yourself; target with the card matching that player's visible ID color; play Ambush to defend yourself.

answers.answer: Knock down the Player ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; those survivors are the ones who participate in the next vote.
answers.evidence: Resolve elimination: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”

answers.answer: If no one wins, deal new central bars face down and keep their values hidden. Since the entire pot was awarded, deal four new bars to make the next central pool of four.
answers.evidence: After round rewards: if the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars; deal new bars face down and keep values hidden.

answers.answer: No. Blue's successful Ambush does not make Purple a Target; the Target is determined by the vote count, and Ambush does not prevent another player from being a tied Target. With four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue is the sole Target. Voters for Purple do not survive on the basis of voting for Purple, since Purple is not a Target; they are outside the winning voting group and are eliminated, absent a successful Ambush of their own.
answers.evidence: Vote: most votes determines Target(s), and players outside the winning voting group are eliminated. Ambush: it “does not prevent another player from being a tied Target.”

answers.answer: The instruction is that tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest point total. It does not specify how to arrange a Showdown among three or more players; the summary identifies this as requiring publisher clarification.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeat as necessary; the source limitation says the cards, procedure, and payoff cover only two players and supply no multiway procedure.

answers.answer: Yes, if the compensation bar gives an outside player a point total that is uniquely highest, the stated end condition is a single player anywhere at the table having the highest total, so that player could be the winner. The summary says in a double-Steal every player other than the two finalists gets one deck bar. It does not specify how to supply the central pot for an extra game-end tie Showdown, but that limitation does not negate the stated possibility conditional on an outside player's total becoming uniquely highest.
answers.evidence: Both Steal: every player other than the finalists receives one deck bar. Scoring: repeat Showdowns until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total. Special Rules notes the pot for extra game-end tie Showdowns is unspecified.
